newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - April 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - April 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
One Bangladeshi Hajj pilgrim died in a stampede following the fire near Mina yesterday, said an official at the Bangladesh Hajj mission in Makkah last night.

Bangladesh and India have agreed not to give shelter to other country's terrorists, like cross-border insurgents. A consensus on this was reached on April 12 at a five-day border conference in New Delhi.

A secret investigation is underway in a bid to unearth the overt and covert bank transactions of Rina Sultana Kibria, daughter-in-law of Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria, in connection with her share business which until recently had remained shrouded in mystery.

Secretary-General of main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan, has blasted the government for what he said "politicising the historic victory of the Bangladesh cricket team in the ICC Trophy."
At least 21 persons were killed and 11 injured, 30 of them critically, in four road accidents in the country on Monday and Tuesday.
About 200 thatched houses were gutted and two people injured when a devastating fire broke out at the labour colony in Adamjee Jute Mills on Monday.

Vietnam said on Tuesday it had arrested the head of Peregrine Capital Vietnam on tax evasion charges, dealing a new blow to a company once considered one of the booming economy's most prominent foreign investor.
Bangladesh is listed among the countries having significant problems in their banking sector.
